item.text:
**Verdict**
Mixed, slightly positive on dignity and equal-opportunity intent, but with clear counterevidence from continued repression and unequal protection for critics, refugees, and some minorities.

**Positive**
- [Statement of Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Thailand at the Summit for Democracy, 20 March 2024](/home/liorshtram/projects/leaders-db/??) - Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand, March 20, 2024. Recoverable URL: https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/summit-for-democracy-statement-2024?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c3060006848. Srettha framed governance around inclusive society, human rights, and multi-dimensional rights, and he explicitly tied the government’s agenda to Universal Health Coverage, Education for All, and the Marriage Equality Bill. IDs: 6B.8.

- [Statement by Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs at the High-level Segment during the 55th Session of the Human Rights Council on 28 February 2024](/home/liorshtram/projects/leaders-db/??) - Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand, February 28, 2024. Recoverable URL: https://thai-inter-org.mfa.go.th/th/content/statement-by-vice-minister-for-foreign-affairs-at?cate=62dfa3b9e5c6102618683d32. Thailand said it promotes human rights for all, humanitarian assistance to all in need, and rights-based inclusive societies that prioritize inequality reduction and vulnerable people. IDs: 6B.8, 6B.6.

- [Thailand: Promptly Pass Same-Sex Marriage Bill](/home/liorshtram/projects/leaders-db/??) - Human Rights Watch, March 27, 2024. Recoverable URL: https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/27/thailand-promptly-pass-same-sex-marriage-bill. The House passed marriage equality overwhelmingly, and HRW said the law would secure equal rights for LGBT people while changing spouse language to gender-neutral terms. IDs: 6B.8.

- [Thailand to be first Southeast Asian country to recognise same-sex marriage](/home/liorshtram/projects/leaders-db/??) - Reuters via ThePrint, June 18, 2024. Recoverable URL: https://theprint.in/world/thailand-to-be-first-southeast-asian-country-to-recognise-same-sex-marriage/2136437/. Reuters reported that Srettha celebrated the bill as a step toward social rights for all people regardless of status, which is direct dignity/equality evidence rather than just aggregate welfare. IDs: 6B.8.

**Negative / Mixed**
- [Thailand: New Government Slow to Protect Rights](/home/liorshtram/projects/leaders-db/??) - Human Rights Watch, January 11, 2024. Recoverable URL: https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/thailand-new-government-slow-protect-rights. HRW said the Srettha government should drop politically motivated prosecutions of peaceful protesters and monarchy critics; that points to unequal protection for unpopular political groups. IDs: 6B.8, 6B.7.

- [Thailand: ‘Swap Mart’ Targets Foreign Dissidents, Refugees](/home/liorshtram/projects/leaders-db/??) - Human Rights Watch, May 15, 2024. Recoverable URL: https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/15/thailand-swap-mart-targets-foreign-dissidents-refugees. HRW said Thai authorities assisted unlawful harassment, surveillance, and forced returns of refugees and dissidents, including deportations without due process. That is strong negative evidence on equal dignity for vulnerable outsiders. IDs: 6B.8, 6B.7.

- [Thailand: Rights Activist Shot Dead in Deep South](/home/liorshtram/projects/leaders-db/??) - Human Rights Watch, June 26, 2024. Recoverable URL: https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/06/26/thailand-rights-activist-shot-dead-deep-south. This does not show a direct Srettha order, but it reflects the continuing danger and weak protection environment in the southern border provinces, where marginalized communities already faced chronic abuse. IDs: 6B.8, 6B.6.

- [Thailand | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism](/home/liorshtram/projects/leaders-db/??) - Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, June 17, 2024. Recoverable URL: https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/thailand. The report says Thai media could still criticize government policy, but self-censorship and elite constraints remained strong, limiting equal opportunity in public debate and accountability. IDs: 6B.8, 6B.7.

**Search Gap**
I found strong evidence on rights rhetoric, marriage equality, press constraints, refugees, and minority protection, but very little direct 2024 evidence that Srettha’s government built equal-opportunity policy in concrete domains like jobs, permits, housing, education access, or disability protections. So the evidence base is better for judging dignity and equal legal status than for judging broad distributive equality in implementation.
